title: A characterization of the sphere in terms of the stereographic projection
summary: Let $K$ be a convex body in the 3-dimensional Euclidian space $\mathbb{E}^3$ and let $N,S$ in the boubdary bd$K$ of $K$, $N\not=S$. Suppose that the support plane $Π_S$ of $K$ at $S$ is unique. For every point $x$ in bd$ K$, different than $N$, we define the stereographic projection $Ψ:\textrm{bd}K\backslash \{N\} \rightarrow Π_S$ of $x$ onto $Π_S$ as the point $y:=L(N,x)\cap Π_S$. It is a well known property of the sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$ in $\mathbb{E}^3$ that the stereographic projection maps circles onto circles (see \cite{Hilbert} pag. 248).
